turns.text: Certainly! Dr. Lee’s work on the "opposite-day" concept involves intriguing experiments where participants are encouraged to do the opposite of their usual routine. One fascinating study had participants reverse their sleep-wake cycles for a week—staying up at night and sleeping during the day. The results showed that while there were initial disruptions, many participants reported feeling more creative and alert later in the day than they normally would. Another experiment involved reversing healthy eating habits; those who typically eat junk food found that sticking to salads and fruits for a day actually improved their mood and energy levels. These studies suggest that breaking our usual patterns can lead to new insights and benefits.
